<thought>
*   Topic: Why Rust forbids two simultaneous mutable references to the same value.
*   Constraint 1: At most two sentences.
*   Constraint 2: Explain *why* it refuses to compile.
*   Constraint 3: Explain *what bug class* it prevents.

    *   *Why?* To ensure memory safety and prevent data races. If two pointers can write to the same memory location simultaneously, the state becomes unpredictable (aliasing + mutation).
    *   *Bug Class:* Data races (a subset of concurrency bugs) and iterator invalidation (memory safety issues).

    *   *Draft 1:* Rust prohibits multiple mutable references to prevent data races by ensuring that only one part of the code can modify a value at any given time. This restriction prevents bugs like iterator invalidation and unsynchronized concurrent access to shared memory.
    *   *Draft 2:* Rust enforces this rule to prevent data races by ensuring that mutable access is exclusive, preventing multiple parts of a program from modifying the same memory simultaneously. This mechanism prevents the entire class of memory safety bugs caused by aliasing and mutation, such as iterator invalidation.

    *   *Sentence 1 (The Why):* Rust enforces exclusive access to mutable references to ensure that no other part of the code can read or write to the same memory location while it is being modified.
    *   *Sentence 2 (The Bug):* This prevents data races and memory safety issues like iterator invalidation caused by unexpected aliasing and mutation.

    *   *Alternative (even punchier):* Rust prohibits multiple mutable references to ensure that mutation is exclusive, preventing multiple parts of a program from modifying the same memory location simultaneously. This design prevents data races and memory corruption bugs caused by aliasing and unexpected mutation.

    *   *Selected Version:*
        Rust prohibits multiple mutable references to ensure that mutation is exclusive, meaning no other part of the program can read or write to that memory while it is being modified. This prevents data races and memory safety bugs like iterator invalidation caused by aliasing and concurrent mutation.
